title: Chapter 36 — The Spouse Delay and The Absent Decision-Maker
intro: The objection that is usually true — and the strategies to prevent it, prepare for it, and close the household.

sections.title: This Is Usually Real
sections.content:
When a customer says 'I need to talk to my spouse,' they are almost always telling the truth. Major appliance purchases are household decisions. Respecting that is professional. Dismissing it is a fast way to lose trust.

The goal is not to pressure someone into buying without their partner's input. The goal is to make the process easier for both decision-makers.

sections.title: Prevention Is Better Than Recovery
sections.content:
The best time to handle this objection is before it happens. During discovery, ask: 'Is there anyone else involved in this decision?' If the answer is yes, explore your options right then.

Can the other person join by phone or video? Can you schedule a time when both can visit? Can you send information they can review together at home?

Remember the Scout Problem from the omnichannel chapter. Technology removes the 'I need to come back with my spouse' friction. FaceTime the other decision-maker during the demo. Include them in real time.

sections.title: The Kitchen-Table Kit
sections.content:
If the customer does need to leave and discuss at home, do not let them leave empty-handed. Give them everything they need to have an informed conversation with their partner.

A printed quote with the complete ticket. Product specifications. Photos or links. Your contact information. A clear summary of why you recommended this specific product based on their needs.

Make it easy for them to sell the decision to their partner — because that is exactly what they will be doing.

sections.title: The Follow-Up
sections.content:
Schedule the follow-up before they leave. 'When do you think you will have a chance to talk about it? Would it be okay if I checked in on Thursday?'

That gives you a specific timeline and a reason to call. It also tells the customer you are serious about earning their business — not just hoping they come back.

sections.title: Coaching Rule
sections.content:
When evaluating how salespeople handle the absent decision-maker, ask:

Do they identify all decision-makers during discovery — before the objection arises?
Do they offer to include the absent partner via phone or video?
Do they send the customer home with a complete information package?
Do they schedule a specific follow-up — or just say 'come back anytime'?

This objection is usually legitimate. Handling it well is the difference between a delayed sale and a lost sale.
